c.tagline: A laid-back mountain valley town beloved by backpackers, ringed by canyons, hot springs, and hill-tribe villages

rides: Scooter rental (the dominant way to get around)

taxi.fareNote: Renting a scooter is by far the most common way to explore Pai's surrounding sights

emergency.note: Tourist police (1155) can assist with English-language support; medical facilities in Pai are basic

religion: Christianity and animist traditions (among some hill tribe communities)
walk: Pai's walking street and town center are compact and walkable; the canyon, waterfalls, and viewpoints are spread out and best reached by rented scooter

safety.safety: Very safe, relaxed town popular with backpackers and long-term travelers
safety.crime: Very low crime; scooter accidents on the winding mountain roads are the more common risk

hood_landmark.Tha Pai Hot Springs: Tha Pai Hot Springs' natural thermal pools
hood_landmark.Yun Lai Viewpoint: Yun Lai Viewpoint's panorama over the Chinese village and valley
hood_landmark.Wat Phra That Mae Yen: Wat Phra That Mae Yen's hilltop temple and town view

avoid.reason: Scooter crashes on Route 1095's 762 curves are the main danger, and party bars see occasional drink-spiking and drug-related scams.

hood_desc: The compact town center that transforms into a lively night market each evening, with most guesthouses and restaurants nearby.
A striking eroded ridgeline a short scooter ride from town, popular for narrow-trail walks and sunset views.
A natural hot spring park east of town, a relaxing stop for tired muscles after a day of exploring.
A hilltop viewpoint over the Chinese settlement of Santichon and the surrounding rice fields and mountains.
A temple atop a hill overlooking the town, reachable by a steep staircase or scooter, with a giant white Buddha statue.
lodging: Wat Phra That Mae Yen-area guesthouses

water.note: Stick to bottled or refill-station filtered water.

transit.sys: Scooter rental (dominant) and songthaews for shared local transport
transit.hours: Not applicable for scooters; songthaews run roughly daylight hours
transit.map: Not centrally published; scooter rental shops are everywhere in town
transit.note: The mountain road from Chiang Mai to Pai has 762 curves, notorious among first-time riders and drivers

transport.air: Pai Airport (PYY) has very limited seasonal flights; Chiang Mai International Airport (CNX) is the main gateway
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Pai
transport.bus: Minivans connect to Chiang Mai (about 3-4 hr on a winding mountain road)
transport.car: The mountain road from Chiang Mai is scenic but winding; many visitors prefer a minivan or motorbike over self-driving a car

airport.name: Chiang Mai International Airport (main gateway)
airport.transport: Minivan or motorbike from Chiang Mai

net.m: Moderate 4G coverage in town, patchier in surrounding hills
net.w: Free wifi standard in guesthouses and cafes
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in cafes
net.ap: An AIS or DTAC tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory but appreciated for guides
